messages:
ana: heads-up: the python quickstart has a couple of issues that blocked a new hire onboarding this morning — the code sample uses client.responses but the package on pip is still on client.generate, and the snippet also fails mypy checks (typing mismatch). link in nav yields 404 too.

rob: ack. which pip version did they use? can you paste the mypy output and the snippet?

ana: it's redwood==0.8.3 (from pip). snippet from docs: 
```python
from redwood import RedwoodClient
from typing import AsyncIterator

client = RedwoodClient()

async def stream():
    async for chunk in client.responses.stream("Hi"):
        print(chunk.text)
```

mypy output: 
```
error: "RedwoodClient" has no attribute "responses" (or "responses" is not typed)
note: revealed type is 'Any'
```

ana: runtime error if they try sync generate: AttributeError: 'RedwoodClient' object has no attribute 'responses'

rob: looks like docs were updated for the beta runtime API shape (responses.*) but pip/stable is still generate/chat. also the streaming code assumes an AsyncIterator return type but stable API uses sync generator pattern.

ci-bot: FYI: docs build failed on deploy at 2026-03-02T07:41:10Z. Error: missing page python/quickstart. Linked issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/issues/739

mike: thanks for the repro. quick plan: (1) revert quickstart snippet to stable API (show both sync and an explicit note about beta async API), (2) add a small typing example that passes mypy for both shapes, (3) add a nav link healthcheck in the docs CI (simple HTTP GET to detect 404s), (4) create an automated snippet execution test that runs examples against the pinned pip package during docs build.

lucy: +1. can we also pin examples to a version tag in the code fence so copy-paste works: e.g., ```bash
# pip install redwood==0.8.3
```

ana: also the sample-app on main references /docs/python/quickstart in README and fails local dev onboarding. I'll open a tiny PR to update the readme and fix the link to the restored quickstart.

rob: please open two issues: one to revert the snippet and add version-note, and one to add snippet-exec tests. tag them devex/docs respectively.

mike: creating issues now: #1112 (quickstart-revert-and-version-note) assigned to rob/docs; #1113 (doc-snippet-exec-test) assigned to devex.

ci-bot: issue #1112 created by mike at 2026-03-02T08:02:00Z.

lucy: I'll take the README PR and link fix. quickstyle: include a short sentence: "The async responses API is available in the 0.10 beta; see /beta for examples." and add a note about typing differences.

rob: landing PR to docs to revert snippet and pin example shortly. will include a small mypy-safe variant like: 
```python
# pinned for v0.8.3
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient()

resp = client.generate("Hello")
print(resp.output_text)
```

ana: thanks — please post the fixed nav URL here once merged so I can update the onboarding checklist.

ci-bot: docs PR 760 opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/760 by rob. Tests: docs build + link-checker started.

mike: follow-up: for snippet-exec tests we should run examples inside the docs CI within a virtualenv and assert exit code 0 and no AttributeError. that's ticket #1113.

rob: merging after green link-checker. will also follow-up with a small RFC for docs linting that validates API names vs published package metadata.

ana: awesome, will re-run onboarding flow after merge. thanks everyone! :raised_hands:
